title: Precision, recall, AUC and the cost threshold

wrong.prf_swaps_precision_recall.py: prf returns (recall, precision, f) in the wrong order
wrong.fbeta_uses_beta_not_beta_squared.py: prf weights recall by beta instead of beta squared, so F2 and F0.5 are wrong (F1 still passes)
wrong.prf_zero_division_gives_nan.py: prf returns NaN when nothing is predicted or there are no positives, instead of 0.0
wrong.auc_ties_count_zero.py: roc_auc gives a tied positive/negative pair no credit instead of one half, so constant scores score 0 not 0.5
wrong.auc_negative_minus_positive.py: roc_auc compares negatives against positives, returning 1 - AUC
wrong.ap_divides_by_sample_count.py: average_precision normalises recall by the number of samples instead of positives, so a perfect ranking scores the base rate
wrong.ap_cuts_between_tied_scores.py: average_precision treats tied scores as separate thresholds, so the answer depends on input order
wrong.threshold_flags_strictly_above.py: best_threshold flags score > t instead of score >= t, so the chosen item itself is never flagged and costs are off
wrong.threshold_swaps_the_costs.py: best_threshold charges the false-positive price for misses and vice versa

hints: Count tp, fp and fn with boolean masks. Guard every division: precision is 0 when nothing was flagged, recall is 0 when there are no positives. F-beta is (1 + beta^2) p r / (beta^2 p + r), guarded the same way.

AUC is a pair-counting statement: compare every positive score against every negative score with a (n_pos, n_neg) difference matrix; wins count 1, ties count 1/2. For average precision sort by descending score, take cumulative true positives, and only read precision and recall where the next score differs (a threshold cannot split ties).

Try each distinct score as a cut with `scores >= t`, price false positives and false negatives separately, and keep a strictly better cost only, scanning from the highest score down, so ties keep the higher threshold. Start from 'flag nothing' (cost = cost_fn x positives).
